--- title: "The exercise" subtitle: "Short" bibliography: [../../references.bib, ../../references-new.bib] --- This page sets out what you do in the short format, and where. The [background page](../../background.qmd) presents the original study, the SCORE replication and the five reanalyses of the robustness study of SCORE [Multi100\; @AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness], and it is the place to start if you have not read it. The session takes Tasks 1 to 4, and you do them in the deck of the session, whose slides run R inside your browser with the data already in place, so that there is nothing to install. The [browser lab](../../lab.qmd), a page of this site that holds the same tasks, is the fallback if the deck does not load. The pages of the two halves say in what order the tasks come. --- ## The claim Five independent analysts reanalysed one claim of the original authors (OAs) in the robustness study [@EinsteinGlick2017DoesRaceAffect]. The claim, as the analysts received it, was: > "Hispanic housing applicants were ... less likely to be greeted by name than were ... white counterparts" (p. 100 of the published article) The published result behind it is the coefficient of the Hispanic names in a logistic regression of a named greeting on the three groups of names, with community controls and the Hard Email indicator: **−0.82 (standard error 0.22) on 549 replies**, which the OAs translate into a gap of **−20.0 percentage points** in the probability of a named greeting, with a 95% confidence interval from −30.5 to −10.0. The data come from an experiment: 1,014 emails to housing authorities, each of which was signed with one of six names that were assigned at random. Your first job is to reproduce the value recorded in the robustness study for one of the analysts, whichever you choose, from the public file of the OAs. Your second is to depart from it deliberately, with a written reason, and to find out what that does to the estimate. ## The five analysts {#the-five-analysts} ::: {#tbl-five .cell tbl-cap='The five reanalyses, with the statistic recorded in the robustness study and the gap in percentage points by the course refit. Source: `data/analysts5.csv`.'} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
Analyst Comparison Emails counted Recorded statistic Gap (points) Conclusion in Task 1
8PTRZ Hispanic against other names replies χ2 = 14.265 −17.3 evidence for the claim
UYV3F Hispanic against white names replies z = −3.771 −20.0 evidence for the claim
EWFMI Hispanic against white names (three-group model) replies z = 3.645 −19.4 evidence for the claim
25N5D Hispanic against white names all delivered emails χ2 = 13.683 −13.2 no evidence either way
P9W8Y three groups replies none recorded −20.0 no evidence either way
``` ::: ::: All five found Hispanic names greeted by name less often than the comparison names, and all four recorded statistics reproduce exactly on the public file. Two of the five nevertheless concluded in Task 1 of the robustness study that the data showed no evidence either way. The analysts compared different groups, counted different emails and used four kinds of test, and the [background page](../../background.qmd#sec-reanalysts) sets out what question each of them answered. --- ## The tasks The session takes four of the five numbered tasks of the exercise. Each says what to do in the deck, and the browser lab holds the same cells as the fallback. ### Task 1 – The setup check The only aim is to reach the point where a line of R runs and the data are in front of you. *Deck:* wait for the engine to finish downloading, then run the setup cell. If the deck will not load, carry on in the [browser lab](../../lab.qmd#task-1-setup), which runs every later task. ### Task 2 – The estimand statement Write the **estimand statement** behind the claim. It says which comparison is made (Hispanic names against which names), which emails are counted (the replies, or every delivered email), and which outcome is compared. The [specification menu](../../menu.qmd) gives the template. *On the slides:* you type the statement in the chat, hold it, and send it with the rest of the class when the facilitator says go. The slides then draw the causal graph of the experiment and show why comparing greetings among the replies conditions on a consequence of the name. ### Task 3 – The reproduction Choose one of the five analysts in the table above and reproduce the analysis from the public file of the OAs, `housing_original.csv` ([codebook](../../data/housing_original_codebook.md)). Four of them have a statistic recorded in the robustness study, from the $\chi^2$ test of a two-by-two table that 8PTRZ ran to the logistic regression of three groups with covariates that EWFMI fitted, and all four come out exactly. The robustness study recorded no statistic for P9W8Y, so its likelihood-ratio test of the three groups, $\chi^2$ = 15.951 on 2 degrees of freedom, can be run again but cannot be matched against the record. *Deck:* the slides have a few cells for each analyst, one step each, and the [browser lab](../../lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction) holds the same cells. When the facilitator says so, the whole class types the analyst and the value that each person reproduced, and sends them at the same moment. Then find out why your number is what it is. `chisq.test()` and `prop.test()` apply a continuity correction to a two-by-two table unless they are told otherwise, so `correct = FALSE` gives 14.95 instead of 14.265 for 8PTRZ and 14.33 instead of 13.683 for 25N5D. The z of EWFMI is positive, where that of UYV3F is negative, because its model takes the Hispanic names as the base group. A reproduction depends on the defaults and the codings of the software as well as on the data and the model. ### Task 4 – The menu This task is **exploratory**. `try_spec()` takes the five arguments of the curve, `comparison`, `population`, `uncoded`, `model` and `adjust`, each of which defaults to the reference specification, so changing one thing means changing one argument. Try several specifications from the [specification menu](../../menu.qmd), one decision at a time, and note which choices move the estimate and which barely touch it. An option that is not on the curve, such as `model = "three_group"`, is refused with the reason given in `menu_options.csv`. `my_experiments()` prints everything you have tried side by side. *Deck:* the slides of the second half carry the cells of the task, and the [browser lab](../../lab.qmd#task-4-menu) holds the same cells. Then choose the one that you would defend and run it once more, so that it is your last try, because the slides place it among the 64 specifications of the curve. The session sends nothing to the class chart. Nothing in this task is preregistered. You may look, change your mind and try again. ### Task 5 – Declaration and report The session stops before this task, in which you choose **one** specification and complete a preregistration block before you run it, and before the class chart, on which each participant puts the specifications of Tasks 4 and 5. Both take more time than the session has, and the page [After the session](after.qmd) says where to take them up. --- ## What counts as a result The session sends nothing to the class chart, and the rule below applies to the results that you send later. A result counts for the class chart if it is one of the 64 specifications on the curve, if it reaches the chart through `submit_exploration()` or `report_result()`, which fill in the class-results form for you, and if it comes with a written reason for each choice; two sentences are enough. The reasons are what make a set of different results more than a spread of numbers, because they show which differences between results come from different questions and which from different ways of answering the same one. --- ## Links The tools of the session: - [Slides](slides.qmd) – the deck of the session, whose slides carry the cells of the tasks and run R inside your browser. - [Browser lab](../../lab.qmd) – the same tasks and their data in a browser tab, the fallback if the deck does not load. The pages of the case study: - [Background](../../background.qmd) – the original study, the robustness study, the five reanalyses and the replication. - [Specification menu](../../menu.qmd) – the decisions of the analysis in three groups, with the options that the curve keeps and the reasons for the ones that it does not. - [Decision map](../../menu.qmd#map) – every decision in the order in which an analyst meets it; selecting an option rewrites the estimand statement and shows the result. - [Specification curve](../../curve.qmd) – the curve of 64 specifications, with the published result, the five reanalyses and the replication placed on it. - [Class results](../../class-results.qmd) – the live class chart.
